text:
ashley: quick heads-up — during the europe-night RAG spike we saw a ~12% absolute drop in prefix cache hit-rate, and tail latency crept up. attaching perf-bot dump below. anyone else seeing this pattern?
perf-bot: automated profile (1987654321) summary: kv_cache_hitrate=58% (baseline 74%), kernel_swap_count +32% vs baseline, avg_token_latency +48ms, batching_coalesce_rate down 18% — full profile: https://perf.internal/runs/1987654321
kevin: thanks. first pass: does the traffic mix have more long-context RAG prompts with embedded metadata? those often blow up key cardinality.
jonah: sampled 2k requests — RAG prompts include an extra `sources:` field and doc-order noise. cache keys are verbatim prompt strings, so tiny reordering => new key. completions workload still shows ~82% hit-rate.
maria: quick repro I ran locally: 1) generate RAG prompt with metadata in different orders 2) observe misses. Example curl:
```
curl -sX POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"convo_id":"c-123","prompt":"[DOC1]\n[DOC2]\nQuestion...","model":"rwd-2"}'
```
flip doc order -> miss. Suggest normalizing doc list or shingling keys.
kevin: +1 to normalization. Also seeing kernel selection thrash in the profile: mixed short (<<256) and very long (>=2048) sequences on same worker -> runtime swaps kernels which costs ~3-5ms per switch and prevents batching coalescing. That amplifies latency when cache hit-rate drops.
ashley: interesting — so two orthogonal issues: key instability causing cold KV cache, and seq-len mixing causing kernel swaps and small batches. both hurt tail.
jonah: propose two quick mitigations for a canary: 1) "sticky-affinity" TTL=30s: pin worker to convo_id so warm KV entries stay on the same device 2) key normalization: canonicalize doc order and drop low-entropy metadata fields from key generation.
maria: also propose prefetch warmup: when convo is first seen, send a tiny synthetic warmup request that pulls the first N tokens into KV (N=8) — cheap but raises hit-rate quickly. We have a short experiment script:
```
# pseudo warmup logic
if first_seen(convo_id):
  send_prefetch(convo_id, prompt_prefix=convo_prefix[:64])
```
kevin: for kernel swaps we should add a binning heuristic in the batching layer: never mix >=1024 tokens with <=256 tokens in same batch; prefer timebound flush instead. This keeps kernel selection stable and increases coalescing.
perf-bot: metric suggestions appended to profile: per-convo.kv_hitrate, per-convo.kernel_swap_rate, per-convo.batch_size_median. dashboard ticket: https://dash.internal/boards/eng-runtime/1987654321
ashley: plan: implement key normalization + sticky-affinity TTL30 + prefetch warmup as 5% canary across europe region; add kernel-binning heuristic behind flag. can anyone own the rollout?
jonah: I can take the sticky + key normalization patch, will open PR today.
maria: I'll land the warmup shim and add an e2e test for doc-order invariance.
kevin: I'll do kernel-binning flag and microbench the kernel-swap overhead.
ashley: awesome. let's meet tomorrow 10am PT to review metrics after a 2h canary. adding perf-bot to post canary deltas. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: noted. will post canary delta snapshot to thread when available.
